title: Comparison of the electrophysiological profile measured by resting-state EEG in subacute stroke patients with and without visuospatial neglect
summary: Patients suffer from a variety of symptoms and impairments after stroke, which may limit independence in everyday life. One very disabeling condition is the neglect. The neglect symptomatology is due to difficulties in directing attention spontaneuosly to the left ore right side of space and body. Neglect occurs more frequently after right-sided and somewhat less frequently after left-sided brain damage. Neglect symptoms are often less severe and patients recover more quickly from neglect symptoms after left compared to right-sided stroke. Nevertheless, presenc of a neglect negatively affect the course of rehabilitation. Different regions in the brain are involved in controlling and directing attention, which are interconnected and form networks to process information. If the networks are damaged by a stroke information processing is disturbed. Brain activity can also be measured in the resting state. In this study, EEG resting state activity of stroke patients with and without neglect (left and right) will be compared in order to explore functional connectivity in left and right neglect patients and their possible contribution to recovery processes.  The results may provide further insight into the differences in recovery from right-and left-sided neglect. For this purpose, the data of patients with left and right sided stroke will be systematically measured and compared at two points in time.
criteria:
Inclusion criteria:
-	Ischemic or hemorrhagic hemispheric stroke (confirmed by imaging).
-	Early subacute phase (<= 3 month post stroke) at inclusion
-	sufficient head control and able to sit
-	Sufficient vigilance for study participation
- Patient should be able to understand the study - with appropriate explanation - and must be able to provide consent. If necessary, caregivers can be consulted to consent for the patient.
Additional criteria for Neglect subgroups: Presence of visuospatial neglect
Exclusion criteria:
- previous stroke
-Patient with stroke in the brain stem with vestibulo-ocular symptoms 
- Epilepsy
- Severe cognitive deficits
- Severe traumatic brain injury, recent head surgery, craniectomy, metal implant in brain
- Psychotropic medications, GABAergic preparations (L-DOPA, SSRI and antiepileptic drugs due to non-epileptic indication are allowed at a constant dose)
- Pregnancy
- History of severe alcoholism or substance abuse, severe psychiatric illness such as depression, psychosis (if not in remission)
